source_name: NLB Skupina – Kodeks: 'Smo družbeno odgovorni' (code of conduct, supplier chapter)
why_relevant: Compliance/integrity section covering supply-chain conduct expectations; the natural host page for any future 'kodeks ravnanja dobaviteljev' and for procurement-integrity rules bidders must accept.

source_name: Intesa Sanpaolo Group – Portale Fornitori (group supplier portal)
why_relevant: Group-level sourcing platform (Vendor Management + Sourcing + Contract Management modules) through which Intesa Sanpaolo Bank Slovenija's purchasing is routed. Registration + Supplier Gate qualification is the gateway to being invited to acquisition events — i.e. the only realistic route into ISP Slovenia RFPs.

source_name: Intesa Sanpaolo Group – Suppliers & sustainable supply chain
why_relevant: Explains the Supplier Gate qualification criteria, Group Supplier Registry and the rule that only positively assessed suppliers are invited to tenders — decodes the process gate for the Slovenian subsidiary and points to the portal.

source_name: Banca Intesa (RS) – Portal dobavljača / Suppliers page (local-subsidiary pattern exemplar)
why_relevant: Shows how an Intesa CEE subsidiary surfaces the group supplier portal on its own local site — strong template for locating/expecting the equivalent page on intesasanpaolobank.si, and useful for cross-border vendor-onboarding comparison.

source_name: OTP banka Slovenija – Politika skladnosti poslovanja Skupine OTP Slovenija (supplier due-diligence provisions)
source_subtype: corporate compliance policy (PDF via download handler)
why_relevant: Published OTP Slovenia compliance policy stating that compliance performs due-diligence reviews of suppliers to mitigate corruption risk in supplier relationships — the only concrete published OTP SI procurement-governance text located. OTP SI now absorbs the former NKBM and SKB books, so it governs the second-largest bank's vendor onboarding.

source_name: OTP banka Slovenija – corporate site (o banki / OTP Skupina Slovenija)
why_relevant: Entry point for OTP SI corporate documents, notices and any future supplier/nabava page. No dedicated procurement or 'javni razpisi' section surfaced in search; the site must be crawled directly to confirm absence and to catch new sections after the NKBM/SKB merger.

source_name: Erste Group Procurement / Procurement Services GmbH (parent sourcing arm for Banka Sparkasse d.d.)
why_relevant: Erste/Steiermärkische-owned Banka Sparkasse d.d. buys through the group's central procurement entity, which runs a standardised supplier-onboarding process anchored on a Supplier Code of Conduct. Slovenian-market IT/payments deals for Sparkasse are likely decided or framed at this level, not in Ljubljana.

source_name: Banka Sparkasse d.d. – dodatna razkritja / razpisi (donation calls) sections
why_relevant: The Slovenian Sparkasse site publishes 'razpisi' only for donations and disclosure documents — no supplier/nabava channel surfaced. Worth tracking as the local disclosure slot and to confirm that sourcing is centralised at Erste/Steiermärkische level.

source_name: Delavska hranilnica – javne objave / javna povabila (document directory)
why_relevant: Evidence that DH publishes 'javno povabilo za zbiranje zavezujočih ponudb' documents under a dedicated /doc/obvestila-javne-objave/ path (observed instance: purchase of business premises in Izola). This directory is where any DH open market call — including procurement-type invitations — would land, even though the visible Obvestila page carries only customer notices.

source_name: Delavska hranilnica – Obvestila (notices hub)
why_relevant: Verified by fetch to contain shareholder, ESG, regulatory and operational notices — the publishing surface from which DH's public invitations are linked. Content observed contained no procurement calls at the time of scouting.

source_name: Addiko Bank Slovenija – corporate site (o nas / obvestila)
why_relevant: No supplier, nabava or razpis channel surfaced for Addiko SI in either language; the corporate site is the only place such a channel could appear, and Addiko's small, centrally-run Vienna group model makes group-level sourcing the likelier route. Must be crawled directly rather than relied on via search indexes.

source_name: Gorenjska banka d.d., Kranj – corporate site (AIK Banka group)
why_relevant: Serbian AIK-owned Gorenjska banka shows no procurement/razpis surface in search results; only general T&Cs and contact (info@gbkr.si). Direct crawling plus watching AIK Banka group communications is the only route to its sourcing signals.

source_name: UniCredit Services (group ICT, operations, real estate, security & procurement arm)
why_relevant: UniCredit Banka Slovenija's ICT and procurement are run through UniCredit Services; no public supplier-registration portal was located for the group, so this page plus group supplier-payment communications is the accessible pointer to how and where UniCredit sourcing decisions are made for Slovenia.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Register subjektov nadzora (supervised-entity register)
why_relevant: Authoritative actor map: exact legal names, addresses and status of every bank and savings bank in Slovenia — needed to build reliable name filters for procurement monitoring and to catch merger-driven renames (NKBM+SKB -> OTP banka d.d.).

source_name: Law Insider – Slovenian 'razpisna dokumentacija' contract corpus
why_relevant: Third-party archive of Slovenian tender documentation and contract templates. Repeatedly surfaced for bank-procurement queries; useful for reconstructing standard Slovenian razpisna dokumentacija clauses, qualification conditions and pricing structures that private banks also mirror.

source_name: Bankart – Sporočila za javnost (press releases)
why_relevant: Bankart is the shared card/payment processor owned by NLB, OTP, Intesa Sanpaolo, UniCredit and Deželna banka. Its press page is where processor-level platform changes, new bank onboardings and scheme/instant-payment go-lives are announced — often the only public trace of an underlying supplier contract.

source_name: Bankart – Letno poročilo (annual reports, incl. English editions)
why_relevant: Bankart annual reports enumerate the ATM fleet composition by manufacturer (NCR, Wincor Nixdorf, Diebold, Diebold Nixdorf) and describe major platform projects — an indirect but datable record of which hardware/software vendors hold the Slovenian processing estate.

source_name: Halcom – Novice / Aktualno (news & announcements)
why_relevant: Halcom is the dominant Slovenian e-banking / PKI / payments vendor (built NLB's first e-bank; serves ~50 banks and 2 central banks). Its news feed announces bank customer wins, acquisitions (e.g. Insite, a CRM-for-banks provider) and payment-reform projects.

source_name: Halcom – corporate history / 30-years retrospective page
why_relevant: Retrospective pages name historical bank customers and national payment-reform programmes (1997-2001 payment traffic reform, 2007 SEPA/euro migration), yielding an actor map of Slovenian banks and clearing bodies to scout further.

source_name: Printec Group blog – banking case studies & customer stories
why_relevant: Printec's blog publishes named customer success stories including NLB Slovenia (contactless ATM reader rollout with Mastercard, executed by Printec Slovenia Self-Service Channels) — direct supplier-side evidence of an award that never appeared as a public tender.

source_name: Printec – NLB case study gated download
why_relevant: Full PDF case study of the NLB contactless-ATM programme; the richest single supplier-side artefact found for Slovenia. Gated behind a lead-capture form.

source_name: ASEE (Asseco SEE) – News & Events
why_relevant: ASEE routinely publishes named contract announcements with regional banks (e.g. core banking + regulatory reporting agreement with KBM banka Kragujevac, a Nova KBM subsidiary; OTP/Vojvođanska integration). Slovenian-owned banking groups appear via their SEE subsidiaries, making this a strong pointer to group-level vendor standards.

source_name: ASEE / Asseco digital banking case-study library
why_relevant: Hosts downloadable named case-study PDFs (e.g. Telenor banka) on a predictable wp-content path — a harvestable corpus of award evidence and a pointer to further bank customers in the region.
